nodes.label: Architecture at a Glance (Medallion Pipeline Diagram)
nodes.norm_label: architecture at a glance (medallion pipeline diagram)

nodes.label: ADR-001: Gold Layer as Fabric Warehouse
nodes.rationale: SQL-fluent team, DirectLake performance without Spark, stored-proc/view support, and a stable relational surface for v2 MCP extension points outweighed keeping Gold on the same engine as Bronze/Silver.
nodes.norm_label: adr-001: gold layer as fabric warehouse

nodes.label: ADR-002: Bronze Sources as Flat-File Drops
nodes.rationale: Flat-file ADLS drop wins on cost, offline-runnability, and production upgrade path (swap generator for real MQTT bridge) versus streaming (Event Hubs) or a REST mock, and matches common OEM batch-telemetry ingestion patterns.
nodes.norm_label: adr-002: bronze sources as flat-file drops

nodes.label: ADR-003: Resource Group Placement
nodes.rationale: The F2 capacity and landing storage were already mid-build in rg-fabric-sandbox; moving to rg-ironwatch-dev would be a disruptive, non-reversible re-provisioning for no functional benefit, so the wrong documentation was corrected instead of the infrastructure.

nodes.label: ADR-004: Identity Model
nodes.rationale: sp-ironwatch-dev and sp-fabric-mal held zero role assignments; sp-ironwatch-dev was granted Storage Blob Data Contributor and Key Vault Secrets User so it can act as the working pipeline identity, while the pre-existing mal-automation identity is left untouched and documented as shared tenant infrastructure.

nodes.label: ADR-005: OREXA Entity Model Adopted
nodes.rationale: The original generator used an undocumented generic CAT-style placeholder spec that risked being mistaken for a deliberate design; adopting the documented, fictitious OREXA entity model (Titan/Kestrel/Ironback, OX- fault codes) gives synthetic data a canonical, written source of truth.

nodes.label: ADR-006: Telemetry Unit Standardization
nodes.rationale: psi (oil_pressure_psi) was a doc/code mismatch and the wrong unit family for an otherwise-metric schema; standardizing on hydraulic_pressure_bar fixes both the unit and the field's semantics rather than doing a naive psi-to-bar conversion.

nodes.label: ADR-007: Spark-Free Compute Architecture
nodes.rationale: On an F2 capacity, Spark's distributed-compute model has nothing to distribute at synthetic-data scale (~375KB largest Bronze file) and its capacity-unit cost is a real constraint, not theoretical; Copy Activity (Bronze) and Dataflow Gen2 (Silver, at the time) keep the whole pipeline consistent with Gold's non-Spark Warehouse engine.

nodes.label: ADR-008: Utilization & Health-Score Redesign
nodes.rationale: hours_operated and service_interval_hours don't exist in the OREXA spec or generator output; rather than amend the spec (Option B), the design was rebuilt around fields that already exist — same-calendar-day oil-sample/telemetry matching and calendar-days-since-last-service for the health-score formula.

nodes.label: ADR-009: dbt-fabric as Gold Transformation Layer
nodes.rationale: Hand-written T-SQL stored procs/views have no dependency graph, no test framework, and no lineage generation; dbt via the first-party dbt-fabric adapter gives Gold ref()/source() dependency graphs, built-in tests, and free lineage/docs, and sets up a project structure a CI review tool can reason about.
nodes.norm_label: adr-009: dbt-fabric as gold transformation layer

nodes.label: ADR-010: Silver as Warehouse, dbt-fabric Spans Silver→Gold
nodes.rationale: Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoints are read-only, permanently blocking any T-SQL/dbt write path to Silver; since Silver held zero tables yet, converting it to a Warehouse before any build work started was a zero-rework-cost fix, letting one dbt project own both Silver and Gold instead of splitting transform logic across Power Query and dbt.
nodes.norm_label: adr-010: silver as warehouse, dbt-fabric spans silver→gold

nodes.label: OPEN-002: No Per-Asset Fault-Event Stream Exists in Bronze
nodes.rationale: fault_codes_raw is only a static 15-row code-definition catalog (fault_code/category/description/severity), confirmed against all 5 Bronze sources and the full synthetic data generator (generate_all.py); no table or generator function produces per-asset fault occurrences (asset_id/fault_ts/active_flag/cleared_ts). The only anomaly concept in the codebase is raw sensor-value drift (is_temp_anomaly/is_pressure_drop/is_rpm_spike in generate_telemetry()), unlinked to OX- fault codes. As a result int_iw_fault_aggregations as originally scoped (join fault events to equipment, hours_operated check) cannot be built. Option A: extend generate_all.py with a real per-asset fault-event table, requiring a new Bronze source and Copy Activity pipeline. Option B: re-scope stg_fault_aggregations as a dim-style pass over the code catalog only (no aggregation), deferring the per-asset fault-event stream and leaving int_iw_fault_aggregations unbuilt. Formalizes a gap already flagged in docs/DATA_MODEL.md §7 (Still open, item 1). Status as of 2026-08-01: OPEN, no decision made.
nodes.norm_label: open-002: no per-asset fault-event stream exists in bronze
